The Gumroad CLI wraps every endpoint below and is built for humans and AI agents alike. Install with Homebrew brew install antiwork/cli/gumroad Or run the install script curl -fsSL https://gumroad.com/install-cli.sh | bash Each endpoint below shows the matching gumroad invocation next to its cURL example. Run gumroad <command> --help for the full list of flags. The Gumroad OAuth API is based around REST. We return JSON for every request, including errors . To start using the API, you'll need to register your OAuth application . Note: The Verify License API endpoint does not require an OAuth application. After creating an application, you'll be given a unique application id and application secret. Authentication On the application page, click Generate access token to get the token you will use with the API. Scopes We've provided the following scopes that you may request when the user authorizes your application. account: full access to most API endpoints. Endpoints with a narrower security boundary, such as media, refuse an account-only token and require the specific scope noted on the endpoint. view_profile: read-only access to the user's public information and products. edit_profile: write access to the user's profile name and bio. edit_products: read/write access to the user's products and their variants, offer codes, custom fields, and files. edit_emails: read/write access to the user's audience emails and read access to the user's workflows. view_sales: read access to the user's products' sales information, including sales counts. This scope is also required in order to subscribe to the user's sales. view_payouts: read access to the user's payouts information. view_tax_data: read access to the user's tax forms (1099-K, 1099-MISC) and annual earnings summary. mark_sales_as_shipped: write access to mark the user's products' sales as shipped. edit_sales: write access to refund the user's products' sales, revoke or restore buyer access, and resend purchase receipts to customers. Resources Create an OAuth application - A getting started guide for creating an application with our API. omniauth-gumroad - (Ruby) an OmniAuth strategy for Gumroad OAuth. More reading If you're interested in learning more about OAuth, here are some links that might be useful: OAuth 2 spec Ruby OAuth2 library Python OAuth2 library PHP OAuth2 library API Errors Gumroad uses HTTP status codes to indicate the status of a request. Here's a run down on likely response codes. 200 OK everything worked as expected. 400 Bad Request you probably missed a required parameter. 401 Unauthorized you did not provide a valid access token. 402 Request Failed the parameters were valid but request failed. 404 Not Found the requested item doesn't exist. 429 Too Many Requests you exceeded the rate limit. Wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then retry. 500, 502, 503, 504 Server Error something else went wrong on our end. To help you further, we provide a JSON object that goes more in-depth about the problem that led to the failed request. Errors responses from the api will follow the following format. { "success": false, "message": "The product could not be found." } When present, the message will describe the particular problem and suggestions on what went wrong. Requests are rate limited per access token: 1500 requests per minute, and a request over that returns 429 with a Retry-After header giving the number of seconds to wait before retrying. API Methods Gumroad's OAuth 2.0 API lets you see information about your products, as well as you can add, edit, and delete offer codes, variants, and custom fields. Finally, you can see a user's public information and subscribe to be notified of their sales. The product is published immediately unless you pass draft=true or published=false . If publishing is blocked (for example, your email address is not confirmed or no payout method is set up), the product is saved as a draft and the response includes a warning explaining why; publish it later with PUT /v2/products/:id/enable . While it's set and the product is published, buyers see it instead of the default product page. Authenticate with a Bearer token that has the edit_products scope. GET /v2/products/:id returns the custom_html field. PUT /v2/products/:id sets it; send null or an empty string to clear it. POST /v2/products/:id/preview_custom_html returns the sanitized HTML and a sanitization report without saving — use it to iterate before you publish. Both PUT and preview return a sanitization_report listing what was stripped. Both PUT and preview return a top-level warning if the custom HTML has no data-gumroad-action="buy" element or gumroad:checkout postMessage. A waitlist form or gumroad:waitlist postMessage stands in for it while the product takes waitlist signups. A successful PUT also returns previous_custom_html (the prior value, for one-step rollback) and the live landing_url . Links to your own Gumroad pages (your storefront, your other products) navigate the visitor's tab as ordinary links — no target="_blank" needed. Links to other sites still open in a new tab. Only the latest version is stored — there's no history, so keep your source under version control. The HTML is capped at 500,000 characters. Rate limits per token: 30 PUT s/min, 60 previews/min. cURL example curl https://api.gumroad.com/v2/products/<permalink> \ -X PUT \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <user_api_token>" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"custom_html":"<main><h1>My landing page</h1></main>"}' Gumroad CLI gumroad products page preview <permalink> ./landing.html gumroad products page publish <permalink> ./landing.html Your HTML is sanitized — disallowed tags and attributes are stripped — then served inside a sandboxed iframe ( sandbox="allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox" ). It can: Run inline JavaScript for animations, scroll effects, sticky headers, and modals. Load scripts from the Tailwind, jsDelivr, and unpkg CDNs. Load fonts from Google Fonts and Bunny Fonts. Load images and media from Gumroad only — e.g. your product's covers and thumbnail. Submit forms in-page with JavaScript. Open links in a new tab or window. It can't: Read your Gumroad cookies or session — it runs on an opaque origin. Touch the parent page. Download files. The sandbox omits allow-downloads , so a link to a PDF, zip, or any other file the browser would download is cancelled — silently, with no error anywhere, so the link just looks dead. target="_blank" does not work around it. Deliver the file as product content and link to the product instead. Make fetch , XHR , or WebSocket requests ( connect-src 'none' ). Load images or media from any non-Gumroad host. Submit forms to external URLs — off-site action attributes are stripped. Every external load is restricted to Gumroad's CDN (images and media) or the named font and script CDNs above, so the page has no arbitrary-host network channel — it can't beacon data off to a server you control. Live values and buy buttons Mark elements with data attributes that Gumroad fills in server-side so the page always shows current values and a working checkout button: data-gumroad-field="name|price|description|rating|review-count" — the element's contents are replaced with the product's current value (HTML-escaped). price is the amount a first-time buyer pays: your default offer code is applied, and a membership is quoted at its default recurrence — matching the native product page this HTML replaces. rating and review-count leave the element's existing contents alone when reviews are hidden on the product or it has none yet, so write your own fallback text inside them. data-gumroad-field="price" together with data-gumroad-option="<variant name>" — replaced with that variant's, version's or tier's current price instead, priced the same way. A name the product doesn't have leaves the element's own text alone, so write your set price inside it as a fallback. data-gumroad-action="buy" — wires the element up to launch the Gumroad checkout. Works on any tag ( <a> , <button> , <div> ). For products with selection state, set the choice directly on the buy element. Invalid values silently fall back to the product defaults — they won't break the page. data-gumroad-option="<variant name>" — products with variants/versions/tiers. data-gumroad-quantity="<integer>" — products with quantity enabled. data-gumroad-price="<decimal>" — pay-what-you-want products; major units (e.g. "9.99" ). data-gumroad-recurrence="monthly|quarterly|biannually|yearly|every_two_years" — membership/subscription products. For complete file state, fetch the product via GET /v2/products/:id and read the "files" array (not returned by GET /v2/products). bundle_products (array) — Items contained in a bundle product; empty for non-bundle products product_id (string) — External ID of the included product variant_id (string | null) — External ID of the selected variant, if any quantity (number) — Quantity of this item in the bundle position (number) — Order of this item within the bundle sales_count (number) — Total number of sales (available with the 'view_sales' or 'account' scope) sales_usd_cents (number) — Total revenue in USD cents (available with the 'view_sales' or 'account' scope) is_tiered_membership (boolean) — Whether this is a tiered membership product recurrences (array | null) — Available subscription durations (present when is_tiered_membership is true; otherwise null) is_preorder (boolean) — Whether the product is a preorder (present only for preorder products) is_in_preorder_state (boolean) — Whether the preorder has not yet been released (present only for preorder products) release_at (string) — Preorder release timestamp (present only for preorder products) custom_delivery_url (null) — Deprecated, always null (present only with the 'view_sales' or 'account' scope) refund_policy (object) — Product-level refund policy override state refund_period (string) — "inherit" when the product uses the account default; otherwise "none", "7", "14", "30", or "183" title (string | null) — Display title derived from the refund period; null when inherited fine_print (string | null) — Fine print of the product-level policy; null when inherited inherited (boolean) — Whether the product inherits the account-level refund policy rich_content (array) — Product-level rich content pages has_same_rich_content_for_all_variants (boolean) — Whether all variants share the product-level rich content files (array) — Files attached to the product. Files whose backing S3 object is missing are omitted from the response. id (string) — External ID of the file name (string | null) — Display name of the file size (number | null) — File size in bytes url (string) — Signed download URL for uploaded files; raw URL for external-link files (filetype: "link") filetype (string) — File extension (e.g. "pdf") or "link" for external URLs filegroup (string) — Group classification (e.g. "audio", "video", "document") stream_only (boolean) — True when downloads are disabled for this file and the buyer opens it in the player or in-browser reader instead variants (array) — Variant categories and their options title (string) — Variant category title (e.g. "Tier") options (array) — Options within this variant category name (string) — Option name price_difference (number | null) — Price difference in cents from the base price (0 for membership tiers, whose prices are set via recurrence_prices) purchasing_power_parity_prices (object | null) — PPP-adjusted prices for this option, computed from the base price plus price_difference; null for options whose price_difference is null (present when the seller has purchasing power parity enabled and the product has not opted out) is_pay_what_you_want (boolean) — Whether this option is pay-what-you-want url (null) — Deprecated, always null recurrence_prices (object | null) — Prices per recurrence interval (present for membership products; otherwise null) price_cents (number) — Price in cents for this recurrence suggested_price_cents (number | null) — Suggested price in cents (may return a number if is_pay_what_you_want is true) purchasing_power_parity_prices (object) — PPP-adjusted prices for this recurrence (present when the seller has purchasing power parity enabled and the product has not opted out) rich_content (array) — Per-variant rich content pages (omitted from GET /v2/products list responses) cURL example curl https://api.gumroad.com/v2/products/A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==/disable \ -d "access_token=ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -X PUT Gumroad CLI gumroad products unpublish A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA== Example response: { "success": true, "product": { "custom_permalink": null, "custom_receipt": null, # Deprecated, use custom_receipt_text "custom_receipt_text": "Thanks for your order!", "custom_view_content_button_text": "Open it", "custom_summary": "You'll get one PSD file.", "custom_fields": [], "customizable_price": null, "description": "I made this for fun.", "deleted": false, "max_purchase_count": null, "name": "Pencil Icon PSD", "preview_url": null, "require_shipping": false, "subscription_duration": null, "published": false, "url": null, # Deprecated, always null "id": "A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==", "price": 100, "currency": "usd", "short_url": "https://sahil.gumroad.com/l/pencil", "thumbnail_url": "https://public-files.gumroad.com/variants/72iaezqqthnj1350mdc618namqki/f2f9c6fc18a80b8bafa38f3562360c0e42507f1c0052dcb708593f7efa3bdab8", "tags": ["pencil", "icon"], "formatted_price": "$1", "file_info": {}, "sales_count": 0, # available with the 'view_sales' or 'account' scope "sales_usd_cents": 0, # available with the 'view_sales' or 'account' scope "is_tiered_membership": true, "recurrences": ["monthly"], # if is_tiered_membership is true, renders list of available subscription durations; otherwise null "variants": [ { "title": "Tier", "options": [ { "name": "First Tier", "price_difference": 0, # 0 for tiered membership options; non-zero for non-membership options with a price bump "is_pay_what_you_want": false, "recurrence_prices": { # present for membership products; otherwise null "monthly": { "price_cents": 300, "suggested_price_cents": null # may return number if is_pay_what_you_want is true } } } ] } ] } } Public product page GET /l/:permalink.json Retrieve the public, display data for a product page — no authentication required. This is the read/display counterpart to the OAuth Products API: it returns exactly the information shown on the rendered product page (price, covers, description, reviews, variants, and social proof), and never exposes buyer-specific, seller-private, or analytics fields. Append .json to any public product URL. https://[seller].gumroad.com/l/:permalink.json Response fields api_version (number) — The schema version of this public payload id (string) — The product's unique external ID permalink (string) — The product's permalink name (string) — The product's name native_type (string) — The product type (e.g. digital, membership, bundle) url (string) — The full public product URL thumbnail_url (string) — The product's thumbnail image URL, if set created_at (string) — ISO 8601 creation timestamp updated_at (string) — ISO 8601 last-updated timestamp seller (object) — Public author byline (name, avatar, profile URL, verified) — no PII price_cents (number) — The product's price in cents currency_code (string) — The product's currency code price_formatted (string) — The human-formatted price display_price (object) — What this visitor would see on the product page: discount applied and converted to the visitor's currency (from their IP, or ?currency=) when checkout can charge in it. Keys: price, price_cents, currency_code, localized, plus original_price and original_price_cents when discounted, and options for products with variants. Tax is not included; it is calculated at checkout from the buyer's billing country. Call it from the visitor's browser: a server-side call returns your server's currency. Responses are never cached. is_pay_what_you_want (boolean) — Whether the buyer can name their price suggested_price_cents (number) — Suggested price for pay-what-you-want products; otherwise null is_recurring_billing (boolean) — Whether the product is a subscription is_tiered_membership (boolean) — Whether the product is a tiered membership recurrences (object) — Available subscription durations and pricing; null for non-recurring products free_trial (object) — Free trial duration, if enabled; otherwise null description_html (string) — The product's rich-text description as HTML summary (string) — The product's short custom summary, if set covers (array) — All product preview images/media attributes (array) — Public name/value product attributes ratings (object) — Average rating, review count, and a five-item percentages array ordered from 1 star through 5 stars; null when the creator hides reviews reviews (array) — Up to five of the reviews the product page shows (id, rating, message, rater name/avatar, created_at, seller response), best-rated first; null when the creator hides reviews. Never includes purchase or buyer identifiers sales_count (number) — Number of sales; null unless the creator opts to show the sales count options (array) — Variants/tiers with per-option pricing and inventory quantity_remaining (number) — Remaining inventory, if the product is limited is_quantity_enabled (boolean) — Whether buyers can choose a quantity is_sales_limited (boolean) — Whether the product has a max purchase count is_published (boolean) — Whether the product is published and live is_physical (boolean) — Whether the product is physical refund_policy (object) — The applicable refund policy, if any cURL example curl https://sahil.gumroad.com/l/pencil.json \ -X GET Example response: { "api_version": 1, "id": "A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==", "permalink": "pencil", "name": "Pencil Icon PSD", "native_type": "digital", "url": "https://sahil.gumroad.com/l/pencil", "thumbnail_url": "https://public-files.gumroad.com/variants/abc/def", "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "updated_at": "2024-02-01T00:00:00Z", "seller": { "id": "G_-mnBf9b1j9A7a4ub4nFQ==", "name": "Sahil", "avatar_url": "https://public-files.gumroad.com/user/abc/avatar", "profile_url": "https://sahil.gumroad.com", "is_verified": true }, "price_cents": 100, "currency_code": "usd", "price_formatted": "$1", "is_pay_what_you_want": false, "suggested_price_cents": null, "is_recurring_billing": false, "is_tiered_membership": false, "recurrences": null, "free_trial": null, "description_html": "<p>I made this for fun.</p>", "summary": "You'll get one PSD file.", "covers": [], "attributes": [{ "name": "Format", "value": "PSD" }], "ratings": { "count": 12, "average": 4.5, "percentages": [0, 0, 8, 34, 58] }, "reviews": [ { "id": "rev_abc123", "rating": 5, "message": "Exactly what I needed.", "rater": { "name": "Alex", "avatar_url": "https://public-files.gumroad.com/user/xyz/avatar" }, "created_at": "2024-01-15T12:00:00Z", "response": { "message": "Thanks Alex!" } } ], "sales_count": null, "options": [], "quantity_remaining": null, "is_quantity_enabled": false, "is_sales_limited": false, "is_published": true, "is_physical": false, "refund_policy": { "title": "30-day money back guarantee", "fine_print": null, "updated_at": "2024-01-01" } } Reviews GET /products/:product_id/reviews Retrieves the reviews shown on one of the authenticated user's product pages, newest first. Available with any read scope. Only reviews that appear publicly are returned — a review is included when the buyer left a written message or an approved video. Star-only ratings with no message are counted in the product's average_rating but are not returned here. https://api.gumroad.com/v2/products/:product_id/reviews Parameters: page_key (optional) - A key representing a page of results. It is given in the response of the previous page as `next_page_key`. Up to 100 reviews are returned per page. Response fields success (boolean) — Whether the request succeeded next_page_url (string) — URL for the next page of results (present when there is another page) next_page_key (string) — Key to pass as page_key for the next page (present when there is another page) product_reviews (array) — Array of review objects id (string) — The review's unique external ID rating (number) — The star rating, from 1 to 5 message (string | null) — The review text written by the buyer; null when the buyer left a video instead created_at (string) — ISO 8601 timestamp of when the review was submitted purchase_id (string) — External ID of the purchase being reviewed rater_name (string) — The reviewer's display name or username, or 'Anonymous'. The checkout name is never used. response (object) — The seller's public reply, with its own message and created_at; null when there is none cURL example curl https://api.gumroad.com/v2/products/A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==/reviews \ -d "access_token=ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -X GET Example response: { "success": true, "product_reviews": [ { "id": "sJ8Yx3d6mUL1kQpVbHnZ2g==", "rating": 5, "message": "Exactly what I needed for my workflow.", "created_at": "2026-03-01T12:00:00Z", "purchase_id": "kL9nR2sTvW4xY7zA1bC3dE==", "rater_name": "Avery", "response": { "message": "Thank you!", "created_at": "2026-03-02T09:14:00Z" } } ] } Categories GET /categories Retrieve the full product category list. Use a category's path as the category parameter when creating or updating products. https://api.gumroad.com/v2/categories Response fields success (boolean) — Whether the request succeeded categories (array) — Flat list of product categories id (number) — Numeric category ID accepted by taxonomy_id name (string) — Short category slug (e.g. "figma") label (string) — Human-readable category label (e.g. "Figma") path (string) — Full category path accepted by category (e.g. "design/ui-and-web/figma") parent_id (number | null) — Numeric ID of the parent category; null for root categories cURL example curl https://api.gumroad.com/v2/categories \ -d "access_token=ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -X GET Example response: { "success": true, "categories": [ { "id": 123, "name": "figma", "label": "Figma", "path": "design/ui-and-web/figma", "parent_id": 122 } ] } Files Uploading a file is a four-step flow: Presign — get an upload ID and a presigned URL for each 100 MB part. Upload — PUT each part's bytes to its presigned URL and capture the ETag response header. Complete — finalize the upload by submitting the list of ETags. Attach — pass the file_url to POST /v2/products or PUT /v2/products/:id . If an upload fails partway through, call /v2/files/abort to cancel it. Abort responses include a status field: accepted means S3 took the cancellation but parts still in flight may finish seconds later, and already_gone means S3 has no multipart session for this upload_id . Call abort again while you see accepted ; stop when you see already_gone . The CLI collapses all four steps into a single command and prints the canonical file_url you can attach to a product: Gumroad CLI gumroad files upload ./course.pdf POST /files/presign Start a multipart upload. Returns presigned URLs for each part. Requires the edit_products scope. https://api.gumroad.com/v2/files/presign Parameters: filename (e.g. course.pdf) file_size (in bytes; max 20 GB) Response fields success (boolean) — Whether the request succeeded upload_id (string) — S3 multipart upload ID; pass to /files/complete key (string) — S3 object key for the uploaded file; pass to /files/complete file_url (string) — Canonical S3 URL ({S3_BASE_URL}attachments/{seller_external_id}/{guid}/original/{filename}); the S3 object isn't accessible until /files/complete finalizes the multipart upload parts (array) — One entry per 100 MB part; PUT the bytes for each part to its presigned_url part_number (integer) — Sequential part number, starting at 1 presigned_url (string) — S3 presigned URL; expires after 900 seconds (15 minutes) cURL example curl https://api.gumroad.com/v2/files/presign \ -d "access_token=ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -d "filename=course.pdf" \ -d "file_size=104857600" \ -X POST Example response: { "success": true, "upload_id": "ibZBv_75gd9o.uPYmGbJ5JjxqK4_VsP3...", "key": "attachments/A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==/9f2c1b7d6e4a/original/course.pdf", "file_url": "https://gumroad-specials.s3.amazonaws.com/attachments/A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==/9f2c1b7d6e4a/original/course.pdf", "parts": [ { "part_number": 1, "presigned_url": "https://gumroad-specials.s3.amazonaws.com/...&partNumber=1&uploadId=..." } ] } POST /files/complete Finalize the multipart upload started by /v2/files/presign. Returns the final file_url. Requires the edit_products scope. https://api.gumroad.com/v2/files/complete Parameters: upload_id (returned by /files/presign) key (returned by /files/presign) parts (array of { part_number, etag }) Response fields success (boolean) — Whether the request succeeded file_url (string) — Pass this as files[][url] when attaching to a product cURL example curl https://api.gumroad.com/v2/files/complete \ -d "access_token=ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -d "upload_id=ibZBv_75gd9o.uPYmGbJ5JjxqK4_VsP3..." \ -d "key=attachments/A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==/9f2c1b7d6e4a/original/course.pdf" \ -d "parts[][part_number]=1" \ -d 'parts[][etag]="9b2cf535f27731c974343645a3985328"' \ -X POST Gumroad CLI (replay from recovery manifest) gumroad files complete --recovery err.json Example response: { "success": true, "file_url": "https://gumroad-specials.s3.amazonaws.com/attachments/A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==/9f2c1b7d6e4a/original/course.pdf" } Don't retry this call. The upload_id works only once. If you lose the response, start a fresh upload with /v2/files/presign and use the new file_url . POST /files/abort Cancel a multipart upload started by /v2/files/presign. Requires the edit_products scope. https://api.gumroad.com/v2/files/abort Parameters: upload_id (returned by /files/presign) key (returned by /files/presign) Response fields success (boolean) — Whether the request succeeded status (string) — accepted if S3 took the cancellation on this call (parts still in flight may finish seconds later); already_gone if S3 has no multipart session for this upload_id cURL example curl https://api.gumroad.com/v2/files/abort \ -d "access_token=ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -d "upload_id=ibZBv_75gd9o.uPYmGbJ5JjxqK4_VsP3..." \ -d "key=attachments/A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==/9f2c1b7d6e4a/original/course.pdf" \ -X POST Gumroad CLI gumroad files abort \ --upload-id ibZBv_75gd9o.uPYmGbJ5JjxqK4_VsP3... \ --key attachments/A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==/9f2c1b7d6e4a/original/course.pdf Example response: { "success": true, "status": "accepted" } Loop on status : while it's accepted , keep calling abort; when it's already_gone , stop. already_gone only tells you S3 has no multipart session for this upload_id — it does not distinguish "fully cancelled" from "finalized by a racing /v2/files/complete ". To avoid ambiguity, don't issue abort and complete for the same upload concurrently. Attaching to a product Pass the file_url from /v2/files/complete as files[][url] on POST /v2/products or PUT /v2/products/:id . The attach step rejects URLs that don't start with your seller prefix. Attach on create (POST /v2/products) curl https://api.gumroad.com/v2/products \ -d "access_token=ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -d "native_type=digital" \ -d "name=My product" \ -d "price=500" \ -d "files[][url]=FILE_URL" \ -X POST Gumroad CLI (upload + attach in one call) gumroad products create --type digital \ --name "My product" \ --price 5.00 \ --file ./course.pdf files on PUT /v2/products/:id is a full replacement — any file you omit is deleted. To keep an existing file, resubmit its id along with its current canonical file_url . Entries without a url are dropped (and the file they point to is deleted). New files may include a client id or external_id (the CLI uses cli-uplo

pages.text: API 10K Discover Blog Pricing Features About Gumclaw Log in Start selling API Widgets Ping API Command line Introduction Authentication Scopes Errors Methods Products Public product page Reviews Categories Files Covers Thumbnails Media library Variant categories Offer codes Emails Workflows Custom fields User Public profile Refund policy Resource subscriptions Sales Subscribers Licenses Payouts Tax forms Earnings Command line Prefer a terminal? The Gumroad CLI wraps every endpoint below and is built for humans and AI agents alike. Install with Homebrew brew install antiwork/cli/gumroad Or run the install script curl -fsSL https://gumroad.com/install-cli.sh | bash Each endpoint below shows the matching gumroad invocation next to its cURL example. Run gumroad <command> --help for the full list of flags. The Gumroad OAuth API is based around REST. We return JSON for every request, including errors . To start using the API, you'll need to register your OAuth application . Note: The Verify License API endpoint does not require an OAuth application. After creating an application, you'll be given a unique application id and application secret. Authentication On the application page, click Generate access token to get the token you will use with the API. Scopes We've provided the following scopes that you may request when the user authorizes your application. account: full access to most API endpoints. Endpoints with a narrower security boundary, such as media, refuse an account-only token and require the specific scope noted on the endpoint. view_profile: read-only access to the user's public information and products. edit_profile: write access to the user's profile name and bio. edit_products: read/write access to the user's products and their variants, offer codes, custom fields, and files. edit_emails: read/write access to the user's audience emails and read access to the user's workflows. view_sales: read access to the user's products' sales information, including sales counts. This scope is also required in order to subscribe to the user's sales. view_payouts: read access to the user's payouts information. view_tax_data: read access to the user's tax forms (1099-K, 1099-MISC) and annual earnings summary. mark_sales_as_shipped: write access to mark the user's products' sales as shipped. edit_sales: write access to refund the user's products' sales, revoke or restore buyer access, and resend purchase receipts to customers. Resources Create an OAuth application - A getting started guide for creating an application with our API. omniauth-gumroad - (Ruby) an OmniAuth strategy for Gumroad OAuth. More reading If you're interested in learning more about OAuth, here are some links that might be useful: OAuth 2 spec Ruby OAuth2 library Python OAuth2 library PHP OAuth2 library API Errors Gumroad uses HTTP status codes to indicate the status of a request. Here's a run down on likely response codes. 200 OK everything worked as expected. 400 Bad Request you probably missed a required parameter. 401 Unauthorized you did not provide a valid access token. 402 Request Failed the parameters were valid but request failed. 404 Not Found the requested item doesn't exist. 429 Too Many Requests you exceeded the rate limit. Wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then retry. 500, 502, 503, 504 Server Error something else went wrong on our end. To help you further, we provide a JSON object that goes more in-depth about the problem that led to the failed request. Errors responses from the api will follow the following format. { "success": false, "message": "The product could not be found." } When present, the message will describe the particular problem and suggestions on what went wrong. Requests are rate limited per access token: 1500 requests per minute, and a request over that returns 429 with a Retry-After header giving the number of seconds to wait before retrying. API Methods Gumroad's OAuth 2.0 API lets you see information about your products, as well as you can add, edit, and delete offer codes, variants, and custom fields. Finally, you can see a user's public information and subscribe to be notified of their sales. Products GET /products Retrieve all of the existing products for the authenticated user. https://api.gumroad.com/v2/products Response fields success (boolean) — Whether the request succeeded products (array) — Array of product objects custom_permalink (string | null) — Custom URL slug for the product custom_receipt (string | null) — Deprecated legacy receipt text field. Receipt text saved in the product editor is returned in custom_receipt_text instead custom_receipt_text (string | null) — Message shown on the buyer's receipt custom_view_content_button_text (string | null) — Text on the receipt's button that opens the product custom_summary (string | null) — Custom summary shown to buyers custom_html (string | null) — Custom landing page HTML for the product custom_fields (array) — Combined list of the seller's global checkout custom fields and the product's own custom fields customizable_price (boolean | null) — Whether pay-what-you-want pricing is enabled description (string | null) — Product description deleted (boolean) — Whether the product has been deleted max_purchase_count (number | null) — Maximum number of purchases allowed name (string) — Product name preview_url (string | null) — URL of the product preview require_shipping (boolean) — Whether shipping info is required subscription_duration (string | null) — Subscription billing interval published (boolean) — Whether the product is published url (null) — Deprecated, always null id (string) — Unique identifier for the product price (number) — Price in cents purchasing_power_parity_prices (object) — Country-code-keyed prices adjusted for purchasing power parity (present when the seller has purchasing power parity enabled and the product has not opted out) currency (string) — ISO currency code (e.g. "usd") taxonomy_id (number | null) — Numeric category ID category (string | null) — Full category path category_label (string | null) — Human-readable category label short_url (string) — Short Gumroad URL for the product thumbnail_url (string | null) — URL of the product thumbnail image covers (array) — Covers for the product, in display order id (string) — Unique identifier for the cover url (string) — Display URL (retina variant for non-GIF images; original URL for GIFs, videos, and oEmbed covers) original_url (string) — URL of the original uploaded asset thumbnail (string | null) — Thumbnail URL for oEmbed covers; null otherwise type (string) — One of "image", "video", "oembed", or "unsplash" filetype (string | null) — File extension; null when no file is attached width (number) — Display width in pixels height (number) — Display height in pixels native_width (number) — Intrinsic width of the source asset in pixels native_height (number) — Intrinsic height of the source asset in pixels main_cover_id (string | null) — ID of the first cover in display order; null when the product has no covers tags (array) — Tags associated with the product formatted_price (string) — Human-readable formatted price file_info (object) — Legacy single-file metadata; returns {} for products with 0 or 2+ files. For complete file state, fetch the product via GET /v2/products/:id and read the "files" array (not returned by GET /v2/products). bundle_products (array) — Items contained in a bundle product; empty for non-bundle products product_id (string) — External ID of the included product variant_id (string | null) — External ID of the selected variant, if any quantity (number) — Quantity of this item in the bundle position (number) — Order of this item within the bundle sales_count (number) — Total number of sales (available with the 'view_sales' or 'account' scope) sales_usd_cents (number) — Total revenue in USD cents (available with the 'view_sales' or 'account' scope) is_tiered_membership (boolean) — Whether this is a tiered membership product recurrences (array | null) — Available subscription durations (present when is_tiered_membership is true; otherwise null) is_preorder (boolean) — Whether the product is a preorder (present only for preorder products) is_in_preorder_state (boolean) — Whether the preorder has not yet been released (present only for preorder products) release_at (string) — Preorder release timestamp (present only for preorder products) custom_delivery_url (null) — Deprecated, always null (present only with the 'view_sales' or 'account' scope) variants (array) — Variant categories and their options title (string) — Variant category title (e.g. "Tier") options (array) — Options within this variant category name (string) — Option name price_difference (number | null) — Price difference in cents from the base price (0 for membership tiers, whose prices are set via recurrence_prices) purchasing_power_parity_prices (object | null) — PPP-adjusted prices for this option, computed from the base price plus price_difference; null for options whose price_difference is null (present when the seller has purchasing power parity enabled and the product has not opted out) is_pay_what_you_want (boolean) — Whether this option is Upload — PUT each part's bytes to its presigned URL and capture the ETag response header. Complete — finalize the upload by submitting the list of ETags. Attach — pass the file_url to POST /v2/products or PUT /v2/products/:id . If an upload fails partway through, call /v2/files/abort to cancel it. Abort responses include a status field: accepted means S3 took the cancellation but parts still in flight may finish seconds later, and already_gone means S3 has no multipart session for this upload_id . Call abort again while you see accepted ; stop when you see already_gone . The CLI collapses all four steps into a single command and prints the canonical file_url you can attach to a product: Gumroad CLI gumroad files upload ./course.pdf POST /files/presign Start a multipart upload. Returns presigned URLs for each part. Requires the edit_products scope. https://api.gumroad.com/v2/files/presign Parameters: filename (e.g. course.pdf) file_size (in bytes; max 20 GB) Response fields success (boolean) — Whether the request succeeded upload_id (string) — S3 multipart upload ID; pass to /files/complete key (string) — S3 object key for the uploaded file; pass to /files/complete file_url (string) — Canonical S3 URL ({S3_BASE_URL}attachments/{seller_external_id}/{guid}/original/{filename}); the S3 object isn't accessible until /files/complete finalizes the multipart upload parts (array) — One entry per 100 MB part; PUT the bytes for each part to its presigned_url part_number (integer) — Sequential part number, starting at 1 presigned_url (string) — S3 presigned URL; expires after 900 seconds (15 minutes) cURL example curl https://api.gumroad.com/v2/files/presign \ -d "access_token=ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -d "filename=course.pdf" \ -d "file_size=104857600" \ -X POST Example response: { "success": true, "upload_id": "ibZBv_75gd9o.uPYmGbJ5JjxqK4_VsP3...", "key": "attachments/A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==/9f2c1b7d6e4a/original/course.pdf", "file_url": "https://gumroad-specials.s3.amazonaws.com/attachments/A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==/9f2c1b7d6e4a/original/course.pdf", "parts": [ { "part_number": 1, "presigned_url": "https://gumroad-specials.s3.amazonaws.com/...&partNumber=1&uploadId=..." } ] } POST /files/complete Finalize the multipart upload started by /v2/files/presign. Returns the final file_url. Requires the edit_products scope. https://api.gumroad.com/v2/files/complete Parameters: upload_id (returned by /files/presign) key (returned by /files/presign) parts (array of { part_number, etag }) Response fields success (boolean) — Whether the request succeeded file_url (string) — Pass this as files[][url] when attaching to a product cURL example curl https://api.gumroad.com/v2/files/complete \ -d "access_token=ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -d "upload_id=ibZBv_75gd9o.uPYmGbJ5JjxqK4_VsP3..." \ -d "key=attachments/A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==/9f2c1b7d6e4a/original/course.pdf" \ -d "parts[][part_number]=1" \ -d 'parts[][etag]="9b2cf535f27731c974343645a3985328"' \ -X POST Gumroad CLI (replay from recovery manifest) gumroad files complete --recovery err.json Example response: { "success": true, "file_url": "https://gumroad-specials.s3.amazonaws.com/attachments/A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==/9f2c1b7d6e4a/original/course.pdf" } Don't retry this call. The upload_id works only once. If you lose the response, start a fresh upload with /v2/files/presign and use the new file_url . POST /files/abort Cancel a multipart upload started by /v2/files/presign. Requires the edit_products scope. https://api.gumroad.com/v2/files/abort Parameters: upload_id (returned by /files/presign) key (returned by /files/presign) Response fields success (boolean) — Whether the request succeeded status (string) — accepted if S3 took the cancellation on this call (parts still in flight may finish seconds later); already_gone if S3 has no multipart session for this upload_id cURL example curl https://api.gumroad.com/v2/files/abort \ -d "access_token=ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -d "upload_id=ibZBv_75gd9o.uPYmGbJ5JjxqK4_VsP3..." \ -d "key=attachments/A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==/9f2c1b7d6e4a/original/course.pdf" \ -X POST Gumroad CLI gumroad files abort \ --upload-id ibZBv_75gd9o.uPYmGbJ5JjxqK4_VsP3... \ --key attachments/A-m3CDDC5dlrSdKZp0RFhA==/9f2c1b7d6e4a/original/course.pdf Example response: { "success": true, "status": "accepted" } Loop on status : while it's accepted , keep calling abort; when it's already_gone , stop. already_gone only tells you S3 has no multipart session for this upload_id — it does not distinguish "fully cancelled" from "finalized by a racing /v2/files/complete ". To avoid ambiguity, don't issue abort and complete for the same upload concurrently. Attaching to a product Pass the file_url from /v2/files/complete as files[][url] on POST /v2/products or PUT /v2/products/:id . The attach step rejects URLs that don't start with your seller prefix. Attach on create (POST /v2/products) curl https://api.gumroad.com/v2/products \ -d "access_token=ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -d "native_type=digital" \ -d "name=My product" \ -d "price=500" \ -d "files[][url]=FILE_URL" \ -X POST Gumroad CLI (upload + attach in one call) gumroad products create --type digital \ --name "My product" \ --price 5.00 \ --file ./course.pdf files on PUT /v2/products/:id is a full replacement — any file you omit is deleted. To keep an existing file, resubmit its id along with its current canonical file_url . Entries without a url are dropped (and the file they point to is deleted). New files may include a client id or external_id (the CLI uses cli-uplo

Digital products, e-books, courses, tutorials, and memberships—almost anything! Creators in just about every industry use (and love) Gumroad, from digital artists, writers, musicians and other creative-types to business-minded entrepreneurs and tech gurus like our SaaS creators. A better question is, "What can't I sell on Gumroad?" What can't I sell on Gumroad? Outside of physical goods, things like illegal or illicit goods or services, securities & financial instruments, credit repair, gambling & lotteries, harassment & extremist content, copyright infringement & piracy, or obscene or adult content are not permitted on Gumroad. A full list can be found here . How do I get paid? Gumroad's goal is to help creators make a living doing what they love, so we make it as simple as possible to get paid. How we pay creators, whether through direct deposit or PayPal, varies by country. What are the fees? Unlike other platforms, Gumroad doesn't charge you a monthly fee. Instead, our fees are deducted as a small percentage of every sale, so we only make money when you do. Can I use Gumroad for memberships? Yes! Whether it's for a podcast, online course, or SaaS subscriptions, Gumroad makes it easy to manage memberships. How does Gumroad handle taxes? Gumroad is your merchant of record, which means we automatically handle all sales tax collection and remittance worldwide. You don't need to manage any tax settings or applications - we take care of everything. What do I need to do about taxes? Nothing! The change took effect on January 1, 2025, and our Terms of Service reflect it. You can continue selling as usual. What about international sales? We'll handle all tax obligations for your global sales automatically. You don't need to worry about VAT, GST, or any other international tax requirements. What happens to my tax collection settings? All tax settings will be automatically disabled in your dashboard. This includes both the state tax settings in your creator profile and any product-specific tax settings. You won't need to manage these anymore since we'll handle all tax collection automatically. Will Gumroad collect taxes everywhere? We collect taxes in regions where we have tax obligations as a merchant of record. This varies by location, and we automatically handle the appropriate tax collection for each sale. Need a Reseller Certificate from Gumroad? Some creators may have an obligation to file sales tax (or other indirect tax) returns already, and will need to report their sales on Gumroad as "sales to other retailers for purposes of resale", which are not taxable. To justify this treatment to your tax authority, you will need to download and save this Reseller Certificate . Share your work. Someone out there needs it.
